I wanted this game to be good. I wanted to love it.
But it isn't and I can't.
It's♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
I don't think it should even be called a "game". It's just one ♥♥♥♥ing QTE after the other.
Let's start with the good:
I truly love the artistic direction TTG goes with their games. I just like it and I feel it fits very nicely.
There are many great characters who you can work or fight with ( or against)
The game has many amazing set pieces and scenes with a lot of potential.
But that's all there is: potential.
The characters are never fleshed out, your interaction with them is totally fake. Except for maybe one or two, NONE of your decisions have any effect on the outcome of the game. There might be some more superficial changes but it's just terrible.
But TTG are lousy at making games. I doubt they even want to make games - they seem to be dreaming about doing movies or tv series because that is pretty much what the're delivering ( and even then it's terribly written).
From the get-go you are on one frickin railroad. You get to have dialogue options and so-called choices but after all the "role-playing" you can do with your choices, nothing actually matters.
Truth be told, there are two major decisions, that actually change the outcome.
One, where you can choose which brother sacrifices himself for the family. And the other where you can save yourself from the headsman by being married/ prisoner to some evil guy.
That might seem big, but the repecussions in the game are pretty much non-existant. MAybe one or two lines changes and that's it.
And then you have the QTEs. Pretty much the only "game"-element in this pile of manure. But they can't even do that well. I don't mind the odd QTE in my games - once in a while. But in GoT you always get those QTE crutches. And not even consistently, at that. They just randomly have you press a random button. Normally, you could expect that one button would be (dodge to the right) consistently but no, not here. If you try to guess what button you're going to have to press you might as well hit one blindly.
And to add insult to injury, about half the time - even if you succeeded in the QTE- you're still getting punished and "lose". So what's the frickin point of those QTEs?
As with the "conversations" those QTEs only give you an illusion of choice. But even that wouldn't be so bad -truly not many games could give you such freedom anyway- IF they wouldn't tout the game with it. That's  false advertising if not plain lying.
The rest of the controls are abysmal as well. You have "w,a,s,d" to walk around, but those buttons don't correspond to the same actual direction your character is walking. For some reason you have a run button - I don't think it works at all and you never need it anyway.
Then you have those scenes where your character needs to "find clues" or "talk to" someone. You get to awkwardly control your character and just try to hit all the obvious spots (you even have a button to highlight all thos spots anyway).
And again, half the time what you do or don't do, won't matter anyway. It's basically just padding the runtime.
Seriously, those old point-and-click adventures did it better than this wreck.
I've said earlier that TTG appear to be trying for a tv series or the like.
But they fail even at that. Their script (their story) is one of the worst I've ever had the misfortune to see.
With - again- the exception of one ot two amazing scenes, TTG has no idea how to write drama. Their modus operandi seems solely to be: What terrible fate could we bestow upon this protagonist now? I know, let's kill their (sibling)/ (child)/ (best friend). Seriously, that's it. Everytime you think: ok finally something good", you can bet your♥♥♥♥♥in the next scene a child will die.
And for no reason other than "It's bad for the protagonist". Many of those deaths make no sense at all, dramaturgically speaking.
After episode one I got the feeling, TTG just wants to utterly frustrate the viewer (you're not playing a game, you're watching a show).
And in that, at least, they excel - I have never been more frustrated than with this skid mark of a title.
Finally, I think this miasma is too expensive for content delivered.

Just when you thought telltale couldn't miss... here it comes Game of Thrones by Telltale, the worst game I’ve played from that company.
There are so many things about this game that need to be addressed, so bear with me and I’m sorry for the long review.
First it all starts with a nice and decent episode where everything seems going in a good way.
However, when the second episode starts that road is lost and now we are on a totally new different ride, from any telltale game I’ve ever seen. The story is kind of interesting but clumsy, the feeling of having a choice is totally gone. I know most of the time it's an illusion in these games however from the second episode until the end of the 5 even that illusion is totally gone.
Well, if it was only that you could still play it for the story, right? Mnhe... not so much. The characters seem well built at first but as the game goes on they start having stupid irrational decisions just to provide you some kind of conflict and make you choose between something. They act like if they were different persons making you feel like it's forced and out of place.
Still in character development, telltale forgot that Game of Thrones before being a game was a series, and before being a series was a book. You can make a game about it but saying the characters you choose to select you have to portrait them accordingly. In this point the game is a bloody mess, every character you might recognize doesn't feel like that said person. Again, like the ones created by telltale, they make decisions that feel weird and out of place just to keep the story going forward. It's an insult for a fan who actually likes the world of Game of Thrones, the only one that got a couple of "lines" right was Cersei and even her got weird at some point.
The final episode picks the mess that were the others and tries to save the game however it was too late. I have to admit that it almost made me give a positive review to this game but when i sat down and thought about it i realized that that would be a mistake from my part.
In my opinion, this episode, was an effort from Telltale to redeem themselves and try to end it with a "bang" that would change people’s mind about this game but it was a failure. Even the end of some plot lines were left opened with "cliffhangers?" something that's unusual in this sort of game. Usually in games like the walking dead and wolf among us even though we feel that there might be an upcoming game, its story stands by itself without needing some other game to hold its hand.
In the end I would give this game a 3,5/10. I like the story but during the most of the game I felt like I was dragging myself in other to reach the end of the game. A disappointment.
PS: I played this game both on pc and ps4, that's why i only have 1 hour and an half on steam.

This is the best Star Wars game of all time and I will tell you why.
First, since the 7th movie was coming out soon, I decided to start playing this game again and I just beat the campaign and played a bunch of instant action. I also played some multiplayer with GameRanger. I now think I can wright a review for this game.
We will start with the pros and cons
Pros:
-Surprisingly fun campaign: you play as the 501st clone division and soon become Vader's Fist. You play in a bunch of the iconic battles from the original series and the prequels.
-All four armies: in this game you get to play as either the clones vs. the separatists (Robots) or the Rebels vs. the Empire
-A lot of Heroes: you get to play as Luke Skywalker, Boba Fett, Darth Vader, etc... There is almost a different hero for a different map.
-Fluent controls: the controls in this game are smooth and it feels good when you shoot rebel scum in the face with your E-11.
-Space battles: The fact that this game had space battles where you can land on the other team’s ship and destroy it from the inside was ahead of its time and no other games captures space battles like this one. There are also different ships for different occasions like there is an x-wing for destroying regular enemies and y--wings to bomb their cruiser.
-A lot of maps: There is a bunch of maps in this game like Endor, Hoth, Geonosis, and much more.
-64 player battles: This is self explanatory
-Modable: If you pair this game with mods you can have an even better time with this game and if add all the user made maps with the ones in this game, there are over 800 maps for this game!!!
Cons:
-Aging: This game is 10 years old and there aren't too many people playing this game on Game Ranger. The graphics are out of date and sadly Pandemic studios went out of business in 2009.
-Unstable: This ties in with the last con. The game has plenty of bugs and crapy hit boxes that will no longer be fixed (varies on each map [user created or not]). The overall function of the game also varies depending on your computer. It will still most likely function properly.
That's about all the cons
Overall:
Star Wars Battlefront 2 is one of the greatest Star Wars games ever made and in my opinion, It is one of the greatest games ever made.
This game gets a 9/10. I highly recommend this game to any shooter fan and every Star Wars fan alike.
I hope you found this review helpful. Thanks for reading!!!

*single tear* Ah, another game genre comes to debunk my bias. A sandbox with a delinquent hero on my command.
Just like with FPS and generally games with lots of violence, Saints Row much like Grand Theft Auto didn't appeal to my eye, until I was offered me the fourth installment of the series as a gift. And oh boy, wasn't it a pleasant surprise.
I love to blow stuff up, and I sure as hell love to do it to those who want to claim Earth, so this was the first step. Slowly but steady, the stunning character renders just won me with their realistic expressions, their lines always keeping me entertained, and it doesn't end there. I'll try to keep this short, I promise.
Excellent story concept? Check. Doesn't matter if it's far-fetched and not one with the real world, it still makes sense as a concept.
Satisfying combat action? Check. Causing mayhem is a piece of cake and with a plethora of weapons and upgrades, beating enemies up is never a tedious task in this game.
Oh, and the vehicles were all really cool. While not being a fan of them in general, the ones in the game were so fun to drive. Oh how I love to perform stunts while driving like a lunatic in a simulation, haha.
Stunning graphics and awesome characters? Damn yeah check. Ascending from a street gang leader to the President of a country sounds so unreal that ends up sounding awesome. In a video game, that is. But the concoction of this category's elements was clearly too delicious for words. How could I not love playing as the supposed President of the USA who pretty much looks like an Australian hippie? Haha, but seriously, Obama, Bush, Clinton, and those before them, I wonder if they ever had to go through similar tasks?
The voice acting was flawless as well, my jaw dropped as I witnessed the credits! Let's not forget the references,
which were a real source of humour for the whole game.
Virtual Steelport looks lovely too, and with all the glitches it's just plain hilarious. As one progresses into the game and crushes the simulated world, it all gets so much more interesting. The character uniforms are eye-candy too, just look at all that purple and the fleur-de-lis badge. Makes me appreciate purple as a colour, really.
Kickass music? Epicly huge CHECK! Not only was the game's soundtrack itself spot-on, but the radio song choices were also ever so upbeat and cheerful! I discovered many new songs to smash the replay button for, as well as have fun in town in my own way. Even my DJ-wannabe self came back to life temporarily. XD
Look at me saying I'll keep this short. Oh well...
tldr, THIS, WAS, AWESOME! So many good feelings, so many good thoughts, I just feel like I had one of the best parties in my life after finishing this game. I had fun in every single second of it. If you're into this kind of games, you've already got this game and most likely beat it
. If you're not, then I still recommend it to you, since it's still a beautiful experience. The Saints Row franchise has earned another eager fan.

Quick Summary Version:
Company of Heroes 2 is one of the top 10 RTS games out there, it's an arcane RTS game with ww2 elements putting the axis vs allies in intense battles ranging from 1v1 battles to 4v4 in multiplayer and got a very mediocre campaign that I won't go into detail. Company of Heroes 2 has changed allot since its early days and is better game if it´s compared when how the game was back in 2013, which allot of people seem to cry about.
The game itself got some of the base building stuff and teaching, though the game focuses more on the battlefield rather than the base building moment of the game. Another thing that company of heroes 2 got that other RTS games don´t have is the RNG element of the game and it´s destructible battlefields that give a nice element to the game.
RNG means random generated number, what it does have to do with the game is to give this risk/reward feeling while you send your units into battle. When your units shoot their guns, the game will select a random number, depending if the number was good or not will determine if the unit made a hit or not. Sometimes a tank shell can destroy a whole squad because of that, and can be very frustrating, but also when you manage to do this against the enemy, it feels rewarding. Though some people might hate this RNG system that relic has added to Company of Heroes 2 as a feature, cause of the frustration it can give while you're trying to finish that last squad or tank and your units miss all there shots to finish the job.
Company of Heroes 2 got allot of DLC that's mostly just skins or commanders that give you a different playstyle, though nowadays relic has fixed the major issues the game had back in 2013 when some commanders were just pay to win, you needed to own these commanders to play decent against others players and the game has become much more stable since then. Relic has also added a "War spoil" system that enables all players that have purchased the game to get the DLC(expect Theater of war and new factions) while playing the game. Though, this system is very close to the drop system in tf2 and is very random. The only really garante for you to get all the DLCs for free is just to play allot over the time and hope you get the DLC you wanted for free. They haven't added any kind of a crafting system with the duplicates you sometimes to get while getting war spoils which mostly leads you to remove them because of the item limit with 1000 slots. They haven't added any trading system for players to trade items with each other which is a bit sad, though it seems like relic is hinting on adding these features with how they drastically changed their business model.
Though, the games got some unpolished features like: how the game lacks an ingame leaderboard to show players what´s there rank and relies more on you using a browser to check your rank from there website which is annoying. The game is also pretty badly optimized and really needs to be worked on. Even the main menu got problems with giving a very unpolished feeling, while starting the game up the screen will lock itself to 30fps cause of the movie that is played behind the main menu.
Another issues is that some animations with the new factions are very clunky and gives a very unpolished feature to the game while playing also, I´m talking about the infantry units animations in the game.
The game doesn't have a option to change your hotkeys which is a bit sad and gives you only the option to change between Classic Hotkeys(hotkeys from coh1) or grid hotkeys.
The ranking system in coh2 is also very unbalanced and will sometimes match you up with a completely new player against players that have 800h+ ingame. Another thing is that they almost never reset the ranks. That means if some player managed to become maybe top 200 or so, it enables him to stay at the rank pretty much with just not playing. It´s a bit shame they haven't really inputted a same kind of a feature that Cs:go got with it´s "accept to play" feature. What I mean is that, when you search for a game and accept, you comply that you are gonna play a game for 30-60 mins, and if you leave, you're gonna get a punishment for breaking the "accept to play feature". This enables players to leave right when a match starts and ruin the fun for other players in 4v4 (for as an example), and make them lose right of the bat and decrease their rank thanks to him/her.
I would recommend this game for people that want something else than Starcraft 2 in the RTS genre and want something new with its own elements. It´s a bit sad that Company of Heroes 2 isn´t really that big in the competitive genre of games, and the game has the ability to be there, though there are some things that need to be changed before it can see that light of day.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a Turn-based, tatical, Sci-fi stratgey game that I was sceptical about going into to, seeing as console ruined my first impressions of this game. When I got into PC, however, I was amazed at how good the game actually was.
In XCOM, you are the commander of a strike team, under the project XCOM opperation, to liberate all the aliens on Earth, and save the planet. It is VERY turned based, and forces you to think on the spot, most of the time, when you are pinned to walls against hostile ailens. The game is also very difficult. Even on normal mode, the game is tough. There will be times when you are yelling at your computer screens to try and tell your team to "learn to aim", and other times, you will hoping that they recieve promotions and don't die.
There are some more aspects of the game, however. You need to manage the research department, to make sure the stuff that you salvage off of the remains of aliens can be studied and more thoroughly understood. There is also the workshop, wheer you can craft items to help your strike team in battle, to help other nations, and to help to fight against UFO's. You also need to manage your crew, make sure they have the best stuff they can, and make they get their promotions.
Overall, XCOM: Enemy Unknown is an amazing game, that I will definitly play more of. This is a game that I HIGHLY recommend to all players out there who REALLy like to think and analize things in games, but also, have a great time and feel satisfied after each victory.

Ever wonder where Blizzard got most of their ideas for the Warcraft and Starcraft games? Look no further than Warhammer. This long-running series started out in the '80s as a tabletop strategy game, and transitioned to computer games not long after. The Dawn of War series takes place in the Warhammer 40,000 universe, and will have a very familiar feel to anyone who has played Blizzard's popular RTS games. No doubt you're already familiar with Space Marines and Orks. You'll find plenty of them here. Starcraft's Protoss and Zerg drew their inspiration from Warhammer's Eldar and Tyranid races, respectively. You'll also find several other factions unique to Warhammer, including the corrupt Chaos Marines, the undead robotic Necron, and the alien Tau. Even during its beta stage NEO Scavenger feels like a completed and a released game. It can be intense (provided you have the imagination), it can be (actually it WILL be) evil and it can be forgiving (for a brief second before you run into a pack of dogmen who rip you apart).
NEO is also ridiculously cheap for it's value. Of course, I'm not trying to encourage a higher price, I'm just thanking Daniel for his reasonable pricing. (Take that Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes)
I can't recommend this enough. After getting the game I sunk a ridiculous amount of time into it in a single weekend. I recommend starting off completely blind. No wikis. No gameplay videos. Just jump in. After dying horribly a few times, you can begin checking a few things out from the wiki. OH and I URGE you to read all the messages at the bottom of the screen during combat (you can click the box to expand). Then just let your imagination fly and get all the horribly violent moments carved deep into your brains. If your imagination is anything like mine, you're gonna find this game to be one of the most ruthlessly violent games you've played and it doesn't even graphically show you any of the scenes.
Now, I understand this is not a game for everyone. If you don't enjoy reading a lot of text, that is not a reason to stay away. You don't have to read any of it. But if you don't enjoy slow paced, the original Fallout-like games with survival and tension, you might as well stay away. But if you know someone who likes that kind of stuff, please, tell them about NEO Scavenger.

Sorry for the 0.1hrs on record, but I assure you I've used it way before it landed on Steam ;)
First of all, I'm happy of their choice, this way I don't have to settle with the packaged version offered by distros (which may be behind with the latest one), nor I should keep an eye on the site to see if there's a new one available.
I've been using Blender since version 1.72b (when it was available for IRIX as well!), and always on Linux, which means I've withnessed the polishing made in 1.80 and the big change that happened with the 2.5 series: basically, they switched the workflow from a 5:4 to a 16:9 ratio due to the diffusion of widescreen monitors.
So, yeah, a big LOL to the noobs/trolls complaining about the UI.
Every new version brought new features, and the big ones got a front seat with the Blender Open Projects:
the respective sites are available at (the name in parenthesis) dot blender dot org
- Elephants Dream (Orange), showing the overall abilities of the software, and focusing on human rigging
- Yo Frankie! (Apricot), aimed to show the potentiality behind the Blender Game Engine
- Big Buck Bunny (Peach), boasting a brand new hair simulator (you know it for being used as demo in A/V commercials)
- Sintel (Durian), introducing the 2.5 series and the ability to make distribuited rendering (The Blender Insitute has its own server farm)
- Tears Of Steel (Mango), dedicated to the new motion tracking and chroma key features, hance being the first Project to blend live action and rendered elements
- Cosmos Laundromat (Gooseberry), greatly improving the hair/particles simulator and aiming to become the first full featured open movie.
Blender includes the features you'd find in a number of different programs in one place, including a movie editor, an audio editor, sculpt mode, GPU Cuda/OpenCL rendering, external renderers support, physic simulators, custom Python scripting for modules/tools, a game engine, multiple file formats import and export tools and so on.
While I've been using it just for fun, all my friends who found a job in CGI/animation claim that they made it thanks to Blender and its flexible workflow, while most 3DSM/Maya/Rhino/etc users only know how to work with the tool they learned.
The Net is full of tutorials for maybe any single existing feature, and the Forums are among the most supportive and helpful you could ever find.
Another important point, maybe the most important one, is the program being free as in freedom: whoever is able to code could take a look at the
and contribute in whatever way is possible.

First off let me say that I have used blender for a good while before I found it on steam, I have used it before and I know how to use it. Its something that I have never been really good at since I never was really into animation/Modeling/Whatever but I have used it. Its a fantastic piece of software, it can do anything you really want it to with a -little- lots of experence and know-how.  Its like Mya and almost can do things just as well or better but the interface is much more counterintuitive than most would like.
Since I saw it on the front page of steam I decided to try it out on steam to see if it was actually the real thing (If they had done anything different from the other versions) and so far nothing is different that I can tell, its on one of the most recent versions and has the same settings and layout as before.
I like using it on steam for the simple fact that it stays up to date.
Really look at the plugins. There are lots of neat little plugins that you can enable that make your life a thousand times easier for doing certan tasks. There is a tool there that adds in a pie wheel for selecting tools that really ought to be added into the program sometime.
How to use it, Blender isn't like other programs of its kind becasue it has different controls than what most are used to, and because of this many get frustrated with the program very quickly and quit before they can fully understand how to use it. The basics are these controls:
1. To select something you must RIGHT click instead of what most people would think which is left click.
2. Movement, to move you use your middle mouse button and drag, this will pan the view to move on one plane instead of orbiting  you hold shift. In order to "Fly" press shift+F to fly this will make you turn around like you are in first person and is useful to know. Scrolling using the scroll wheel while flying speeds up and slows down your movement.
3. Rendering, to render a scene from the view of your camera press F12 this will start the render once its done/while rendering hit ESC to stop the rendering at any time. you can also hit SHIFT+Z to render in real time, but as a forwarning don't do this if you have a bad computer or you have a lot going on in your scene as it will crash or freeze and nobody wants that
4. Editing objects, in order to do basic objects hit SHIFT+A to add objects to your scene. Hit TAB to enter edit mode to edit the objects. right click on the points in the corners to select these points and hit G to grab them. Press E to Extrude those verticies. R to rotate the object or selected verticies. S to scale the object or selected verticies. (Verticies being the individual points in the object)
5. Help, If you need help look it up on youtube, there are lots of tutorials that you can watch for free and plenty of paid courses too. Press the SPACEBAR to search a function that you can do, if it has a keybinding then it will show it next to it.
6.
Overall I would rate this:
Ease of access: 7/10, its a hard to learn program but once you learn how to use it its a great program
Preformance: 9/10, this is continually being updated and it runs well if you have a good computer
Usefulness: 10/10, it can do almost anything you want it to inside of the program, there isn't much that you really have to do outside of the program other than adding in things like camera flares, etc.
I will edit this in the future if I see something that I need to add.

As depressing as it is to write this, I simply cannot give this game a reccomendation. I'm a huge fan of both Telltale games, and HBO's Game of Thrones series (I haven't read the books) and when announced, this game seemed fantastic. When my girlfriend gifted me it, I was excited to play it alongside her. Needless to say, we were disappointed.
Without going into too much detail, the choices felt hollow. Of course, that's nothing new with story driven games; there will always be fixed points which your choices will revolve around. As wonderful as it would be to have each choice branch off into a new story, I appreciate that such a task would take a good number of years, and each storyline may suffer for the number of others; the quality may be spread thin. With this in mind, however, I had hoped, at least, that the relatively linear story would be worthwhile.
Unfortunately, I feel this wasn't the case. Ignoring spoilers, from what I can see, it's impossible to get a happy ending. I understand that many may defend the writers on this as Game Of Thrones isn't known for being a 'Sunshine and Rainbows' kind of world. Nevertheless, I would have hoped that it would be possible. If all the endings are nearly identical, what's the point of the story in the first place? After dozens of choices, some characters will live, no matter how ridiculous it is. In other instances, I have gone out of my way to attempt to have a character killed, or at least dislike me, to no avail; when it says 'X will remember that', they won't. They never will. I literally left two different characters to die at different points in the game, and when they miraculously didn't die, they were mildly annoyed for a single scene. Beyond that, we were the best of friends once more (much to my frustration).
Towards the end, things began to feel slightly less useless (A common theme throughout this title) as your choices began to take effect. You gained a sense of hopefulness, and it was all for naught. No matter how many soldiers you somehow recruit, or how deviously you play the metaphorical game of thrones, it doesn't matter. You won't get the happy ending you crave after your 14~ hours of gameplay. (My own playthrough was a tad longer due to my frequent rants complaining about outcomes of choices).
All of this is without mentioning the numerous issues I had with running it. I appreciate my PC isn't the greatest, so it may well be simply my own fault. If that is the case, feel free to disregard this. Many times, the game would crash for no apparent reason. Other times, the cursor would disappear following me pausing the game, and every so often there would be audio/visual glitches. Again, the technical issues may rest with me.
Overall, if I had to give this a rating, I would be tempted to aim around the 3/10 margin. As usual, the indescribable telltale charm was present, however hidden it was by the glaring plot/gameplay issues. The voice actors, for the most part, were brilliant as expected, ignoring a few odd, awkward deliveries. Those from the TV show's cast performed well, and I would like to give special praise to Iwan Rheon's Ramsay Bolton. He is just as sadistically manic as his show's portrayal, and whenever he appeared on screen, I couldn't help but grin. I knew that, whatever ridiculous plot followed, he'd make the coming moments enjoyable.
With the recent news that Telltale's season 2 of Game of Thrones is 'on hold', I hope this may hint that they are taking their time with the story, rather than pumping out a sequel; the end held many, deliberately open ends to ensure a follow-up purchase for the next game. With 'Minecraft: Story mode - Season Two' steadily being released, though, who knows?

"Do not get caught with your pants down. Pants? You start the game with no pants at all!"
Oh dear...
The game offers a good demo -
so there's no cost to trying it out. The UI is bad, but the lure of trying again, and trying to learn and make progress is there, and it is strong. You will almost certainly not be impressed the first time you play it, but give it a second or third chance. It plays differently and presents a very interesting and realistic, though grim and unfair world to explore.
I have enjoyed a lot of games that focus on sneaking and hiding but few made simple hiding as desperate or exciting as NEO Scavenger. You try desperatly to cover your tracks and hide before you end your turn. But that slows your progress... Hunger, thirst and the bitter cold force you to take risks. Plus you need stuff to survive, but unfortunatly for you, so do other drifters and vagabonds.
Combat is unbelivably intense. UI clunkiness robs us of the full experience at least the first few times, then it becomes less about the menus and more about your, so far well going game, about to be ruined by a stranger. Even a weaker oponent can cause harm, wounds, and can alert other threats and lead them to you. There is no time pressure of any kind during combat, yet it allways feels dangerous or even desperate. You have to have some degree of faith that your choices will play out in your favor. They usually lead to your death until you learn more about the game. It's very much about survival, staying safe, luring other threats into traps or each other... and scavenging. Remains, food, parts. You're allways scavenging and the overall aim is to set yourself up for survival.
First impressions count for a lot, and this game is Early Access which hurts it somewhat, esp. the lack of variety in a game where you die and start over so much. NEO Scavenger attempts to offer a niche gameplay experience, a bit like FTL or Papers, Please, where gameplay and style are different enough to make it something unique. Unfortunatly, it's current Early Access status makes it clumsier and less satisfying to play, and promises such as "This isn't even my final form!" usually end up dissapointing. However, this could be a very good game and trying the demo wont cost you a thing.
Recommended for fans of turn based combat, realism, crafting, survival, adventures, Fallout, and games where graphics take a back seat to gameplay, strategy and athmosphere.

I'm not very picky with what I play, but I am picky with what I play often. Since I got it, I have been playing this game every day, dieing every day, and starting anew every day. You die, a lot. But for some reason I always come back to start again, most times directly after the fact. This isn't like Dark Souls difficult, where if you die, you can just load up a save from right before it. No. When you die, you die. You have to start all over again.
Each time you start, it is somehow an entirely new experience every time. The maps are randomized, NPC loadouts are randomized, loot and scavenging opportunities are randomized. The only things that don't change are the story, fixed encounters, and your inevitable death in these unforgiving wastes. You can spend hours building up the best loot and getting the best weapons and armor, just to get kicked in the head in your sleep, and have to start all over again. For some reason I have come to enjoy this.
The crafting system is remarkable, to say the least. Much more involved than that of Minecraft or Terraria. You are able to use the skills you chose at the start of the game to create new and different items than you could without. Being able to craft items that can possibly save you from a fight with a Dogman or a Blue Frog, keep you fed for a day, or drink clean water, can give you some sense of security. Until you fall asleep and get kicked in the head.
This game is not for those that want an easy game, that they can win every opportunity they get. You can be fully armored and have a shotgun in one hand and a crowbar in the other and pulverize the person you're fighting, just to have them throw a rock at you and die of internal bleeding a couple turns later. This game is unforgiving, and even when you're the biggest badass of the wastes... you can still die by eating some berries.
I love this game. Plain and simple.

This is the best Star Wars game of all time and I will tell you why.
First, since the 7th movie was coming out soon, I decided to start playing this game again and I just beat the campaign and played a bunch of instant action. I also played some multiplayer with GameRanger. I now think I can wright a review for this game.
We will start with the pros and cons
Pros:
-Surprisingly fun campaign: you play as the 501st clone division and soon become Vader's Fist. You play in a bunch of the iconic battles from the original series and the prequels.
-All four armies: in this game you get to play as either the clones vs. the separatists (Robots) or the Rebels vs. the Empire
-A lot of Heroes: you get to play as Luke Skywalker, Boba Fett, Darth Vader, etc... There is almost a different hero for a different map.
-Fluent controls: the controls in this game are smooth and it feels good when you shoot rebel scum in the face with your E-11.
-Space battles: The fact that this game had space battles where you can land on the other team’s ship and destroy it from the inside was ahead of its time and no other games captures space battles like this one. There are also different ships for different occasions like there is an x-wing for destroying regular enemies and y--wings to bomb their cruiser.
-A lot of maps: There is a bunch of maps in this game like Endor, Hoth, Geonosis, and much more.
-64 player battles: This is self explanatory
-Modable: If you pair this game with mods you can have an even better time with this game and if add all the user made maps with the ones in this game, there are over 800 maps for this game!!!
Cons:
-Aging: This game is 10 years old and there aren't too many people playing this game on Game Ranger. The graphics are out of date and sadly Pandemic studios went out of business in 2009.
-Unstable: This ties in with the last con. The game has plenty of bugs and crapy hit boxes that will no longer be fixed (varies on each map [user created or not]). The overall function of the game also varies depending on your computer. It will still most likely function properly.
That's about all the cons
Overall:
Star Wars Battlefront 2 is one of the greatest Star Wars games ever made and in my opinion, It is one of the greatest games ever made.
This game gets a 9/10. I highly recommend this game to any shooter fan and every Star Wars fan alike.
I hope you found this review helpful. Thanks for reading!!!

I saw this game on sale for less than a buck and said "hey, why not?"  That was probably the best decision I made that day because I am getting way more than my money's worth out of it and I can say without a doubt that it is worth more than its full price.  Granted, this is not some Earth-shattering monument of technical achievement or anything.  But for what it is, it is very fun and will provide you with hours of amusement.  For an idea of what the game itself is like, imagine Oregon Trail meets Galaga as written by Tim & Eric and directed by Mel Brooks (because that totally doesn't sound like some kind of monster).  The gameplay itself is smooth, fun, and well-varied.  Most of the things that you come across are pretty much random events (there is some overall structure; i.e. you generally pass through most of the same 'zones' in the same order, however what those 'zones' contain tends to be randomized), and there are some very interesting (and amusing) random events.  Controls are simple and responsive and it's controller-compatible, so you've got options there.  There are also a bunch of unlockables to keep you engaged for a while, including different modes of play (sadly, however, no multiplayer).
Overall, this game is a really great deal if you like retro-styled side-scrolling shooter games with a heavy helping of humor.  Get it.  Play it.  Enjoy it.

Saints Row IV is an insanely realistic military shooter. You are a member of the Saints, a secret french special operations unit. You go into situations that even the GIGN are not prepared for. All the weapons are incredibly realistic, very well researched and you can nearly feel the recoil. Your operations are well plotted out and you really feel like a member of a special ops unit. You never feel overpowered, and you truly fear the brutal power of you enemy's bullets. This game has an extremely tight grip on reality.The conflict is generated when a british, shakespeare-loving politician is attacked by a street gang for supporting Prof. Genki. Genki is a geneticist, and some are opposed to his experiments. This game offers a very meaningful look at bioethics, and on how flawed our military conflicts are. I was crying at the end when SPOILER ALERT!!!!!!! you have the option to let Genki kill the leader of the gang, or execute Genki. I regretted my choice, but I knew it was better than the alternative. At the end, I would give it 10/10.

You are El Presidente, a dictator that has his, or hers, own topical nation island. The game has a lot of charm and humor, which you can see all over the place. Gameplay is not made for large scale sandbox playing, instead it's heavily oriented towards the campaign missions, but don't worry, here, it has you covered. The "Modern Times" expansion brings a lot to the table, like new buildings and a new campaign. The campaigns follow a story and you get to do all sorts of crazy stuff including getting (Twitter?) followers and managing a hiccup outbreak. Every person on the island is tracked individually, you can click on them and see all sorts of data and their thoughts. Here you can also issue arrest warrants, bribes, brand them as heretics, eliminate or arrange "accidents".
Unfortunately not everything is happy and sunny, there is a lack of micro-management that I believe is necessary. For instance I had a pretty big problem when instead of exporting what I considered excess food, my subjects decided to first hoard a lot of the food at the market instead of a more balanced approach. "Modern Times" times comes with a lot of newer versions for a lot of buildings, unfortunately you're stuck with a pretty inefficient system for the transport of goods, which becomes a bigger and bigger bottleneck as your city develops.
Pros: charm and humor.
Cons: doesn't scale well for larger cities, lack of some management options.
Rating: Have no fear, El Presidente is here!

Did you enjoy Diablo II?  Then you should love Grim Dawn.  While it's not exactly brimming with creativity it has taken a ton of elements that we love from Diablo and it's clones, improved upon them, and added it's own ideas to the mix, and as a result has made a highly refined and fun game that they're still upgrading and tweaking as of the time I'm typing this review.

Enjoy the story while you're at it.  Speaking of the story there's tons of little tidbits throughout the game such as letters, quests, and whatnot that tell you about the world of Grim Dawn, it's factions, and help you immerse yourself in the setting.
Oh and they recently released an expansion for this.  A proper expansion adding a new chapter, new classes, and whatnot.  I've started working through the game again with one of the new classes so as of right now I can't say much about the new chapter itself but one of the new classes I'm trying(Necromancer) is fun to play as so far as I summon swarms of the undead to assist me. Dawn of War still holds up as a fun, fast paced RTS game today. The multiplayer is perhaps improved in Dark Crusade so I'll discuss the singleplayer campaigns.
The original campaign is lax, ultimately pretty boring except for the odd exception. It is essentially a tutorial for playing the game and specifically the Space Marines. It also is a prelude to all the later Blood Ravens stuff in Dawn of War 2.
However the Winter Assault campaign really shines above all others; this has so many inventive additions and interesting objectives that it shines above almost any other RTS game's past and present. Frankly unless it is an open world RTS (ala Total War) more games should have fluid changing between multiple sides on one map, maps with multiple optional objectives, each mission being drastically different yet retaining the core RTS elements!
The writing is good, a plot that makes sense with armies acting much more in character then most of the time. Brilliant fun!
Very, VERY solid game except for some minor bugs which are mostly fixed by patches. One of the few games that will take your hours, make you lose and still make you come back for more.

I don't have much time playing this, but whenever I do boot it up it never ceases to be worth my time. Out of all the games, I guess that Poker Night is what puts me through a rollercoast of emotions the most. I get bummed out, I get super happy, I start getting cocky and then I am reminded of my humbleness by Heavy and his horseapple hand.
What I most like about this game is that it has some things that few single-player poker games have: different AIs and bluffs. If you pay enough attention, you can figure out the different playstyles of your opponents, whether the hand is good or not for them and even if they are bluffing.
And like every poker game, a lot of weird stuff happens here too. For example, this last tournament I was in: one of the hands consisted in a flush. On the table. Everybody gets a flush. YOU get a flush! And YOU get a flush!
But I had the ace so I won the hand.
On the same tournament, it was down to me and Max. Max had 500 dollars. I won with an ace high.
Insane things like these is what makes Poker Night at the Inventory a remarkable card game, and if you love yourself some poker and you do not have the money to splurge on actual tournaments, I sincerely reccomend this to you. I bought it a couple of summer sales ago along with its sequel and "Papers, Please" for the grand total of 20 reais (about 10 dollars). Even if it's not summer sale, I'd say this game is worth its price.
Some things that do upset me a little are the little sound bugs here and there, and sometimes it does freeze as if it is thinking. Also the mouse sensibility is stupendously weird and no matter how much I fiddle with the settings I can't get it to work normally. I guess my mouse will be drunk forever whenever I'm playing this game.
Also, the subtitles censor the word t w a t. I don't find that upsetting, I just find it unnecessary.
O sweet nostalgia, this game tickle me right way :D

Wow... what to say about XCOM: Enemy Unknown? It took me 36 hours to complete the game (after one false start), and that day and a half I devoted to saving planet Earth was so incredibly fun that I had a hard time putting it down (just one more turn... just one more mission...). And so incredibly frustrating... yet somehow, even when I ragequit because I did something stupid and got one of my soldiers killed, I was back up and playing within 15 minutes because I wanted to keep playing.
XCOM:EU is a turn-based tactics game, which means you have to plan ahead and play things smart if you want to keep your squad alive. And even if you come up with the perfect strategy, odds are, something will go terribly wrong and your soldiers will die a terrible death anyway (and you might get attached to your soldiers, so don't do that). Even though it isn't a fast-paced game, boy, does it get tense sometimes. Personally, I find real-time strategy games a bit overwhelming, so it struck a perfect balance for me.
I play on a rather low-end system (integrated Intel HD 400 graphics on a i3 processor) and the game ran great, barring a few choppy cutscenes. Always a plus.
I loved being able to customize my soldiers, although I wish there were a few more choices... after a while, everyone started to look and sound the same despite my best attempts to avoid it. The Enemy Within expansion included a bunch of foreign language voices to pick from, which helps break the monotony).
The story was very enjoyable. I know a lot of people felt that XCOM:EU was too "on the rails", but I like that the game was driven forward by plot events. It didn't feel rushed or too drawn out, especially with the missions and plotlines added in the DLC (Admittedly, I feel like some parts could have been developed further-- mae a bit more in-depth).
I wish there were more games done in the style of XCOM:EU, because I love the genre, the gameplay, and the concept of controlling my own little squad and watching them progress and grow stronger (and cry when they are mauled by a pack of Chrysalids and gunned down by their mind-controlled squadmate... but I digress).
XCOM:EU was my first foray into the world of XCOM, having never played any of the original games released in the 90s. So I can't really say how XCOM:EU compares to the other titles in the series. There was no nostalgia for me; XCOM was a brand new experience for me (I have played Xenonauts, but it's like comparing homemade cookies to an ice cream sundae. One is a little fancier, but they are both really good; it just depends on what you are in the mood for). And what an experience it was... possibly one of my favorite games. If you have not tried it yet, and are intrigued by the idea of blasting aliens of the planet or like squad-based games... really, give it try.

I spent a lot of time looking for a good scavenging/crafting/surviving experience. Since stalker: call of pripyat I felt kind of left in the bench, but Neo scavenger totaly have potential for it! It feels like actual surviving, having to find food, clothes, shelter, water, tools, weapons, decide if you run or fight in an encounter, craft things etc. every mistakes can be paid the high price, the global experience is impressively convincing!
The game's really hard tho, I keep dying in so many different ways, which is great as surviving shouldn't be easy, but the permadeath makes it really hard on the player, you barely start to get some good stuffs and die to start from the beghining again. It's really frustrating, but the difficulty of the game make it so deliciously painful ^^
The game is still on developement so criticizing is probably prematured, but i'd like to signal that the rarity and price of ammunitions makes it unworthy to equip anything else than melee weapons, also (maybe it's a bug) when the cart broke i lost all my stuffs inside on many occasions, which doesn't make sens, as if the cart broke the stuffs shouldn't just disapear and be on the ground for me to save what i can... And last thing, the food/water mechanism isn't really logic, as you'll starve almost as fast as you'll get dehydrated, eating 50kg of berries will feed you for barely a few hours and they're pretty hard to find when you need them.
Here's a few thing I'd love to see implemented/improved, hopefully devs would read it (who knows ^^) and find some indeas interesting, also maybe some things i suggest here are allready in the game/planed and I haven't found out yet, sorry if it happen:
-Ability to cancel last action, as sometime i click on the wrong square or make mistakes while crafting.
-Fixing the strarvation system: human body can last over 40 days without food, it doesn't make sense to die from starvation after barely 2 days. Maybe splitting "well fed" with "hungry" and "bulk", where "hungry" would affect your action points, fight capability, scavenging ability etc. While "bulk" would be your global "well fed" status, going from overweight (which inflict handicap), to anorexic which make "hunger" constantly low and starvation deadly. Also the meat spoils really fast, i'm not sure if it's unrealistic but why not some ways to make it last longer, like an hermetic bag, lunch boxes, thermal backpack or something.
-The combat interface is pretty hard to understand, sometime i just get attacked out of nowhere while sleeping (which is pretty cool), but the guy turns out to be badly stuffed and wreck me out in couple hits, leaving me no other option than crie while watching my character die in horrible pain. Maybe something signaling the global risk of the oponent and/or chances of successfull attacks, dodges, escapes etc. Just so we know if we can try a fight or just drop all our ♥♥♥♥♥ out and run the hell away.
-How can't a medic + botanic find some antidotes in forests? I keep dying from poisoning without having any chance of reaching the clinic. Also, items in general lacks a description of their effects as well as statuses leave you wondering how to fix them i'd like to have a hint of what everything does or need to be fixed (for ex: antibiotics: can heal X, or dissentry: can be healed with X).
-When crafting, have a picture of each craftable item in the recipes list, this would ease a lot the recipe's browsing.
-Pliz, just pliz, more ammunitions, I gave up using any weapon as i take hours to find only 3 bullets, and allways for the one weapon you don't have, i love to shoot things, but in a week of playing I had the chance to do so about 3 times only.
-I would LOVE to be able to fix items, for example taking parts of one gun to fix another gun, it makes a lot of sense and have been seen in many crafting/rogue-like games (such as fallout or 7days to die), I really love that feature as you don't waste good finds (like guns, backpacks, carts etc...) just because you allready have one that's in a barely better condition.
-More shopz! there is only one shop, and it's near town which mean if you want to farm cash, buy ammunitions, buy food etc. You'll have to go all the way there, across that lifeless desert of empty buildings and rude people that won't let you kill and eat them, I died a LOT starving just trying to reach it, why not itinerant sellers or random shops in some ruins?
-Ability to settle. I mean it's a surviving game, greatly done, but you can't make you home anywhere, why not the ability to choose a place to fortify, stock food, make confortable shelter, medical supplies, and (why not) working benches that allows you to fix things, craft more, that require tools to enable some special crafts etc.
-Definitly more scavenging places, and more specifics ones, like pharmacies, gunshops, supermarkets, factories... We all love those.
-Reinforce the "friendly encounters" potential, right now it's mostly neutral/ennemy, maybe we could meet some people that help us, offer trades, indicate to locations etc.
-The ability to loot money from innocent victi... people i killed in legitimate defense, I mean there is money in the game, how come no one carry any?
-More weapons and more craftability in weapons, like the ability to upgrade a rifle (kind of like in stalker, i really loved that feature) to make it more deadly. Also the ability to craft bullets would be nice.
-Skill learning, I don't get why there is so much slots available while you can't chose more than 5 to about 8 skills, i get it for the start, but then i'd like to have a way to learn new skills ingame after a while.
-Even biger map. I know this one is huge allready, but in the end there's nothing but one city and the start facility (plus the ruins of course) I'd love to see more special places, more terrains, more climates... more surprises!
-More hunting potential, I managed to kill a dear once, but with no ammunitions and no way to come near them and oneshot them, it's really hard to get any, so the moral choice of rather eating or not human flesh become a rethorical question: you just can't survive without your daily bad mutha's barbecue, I'd like to play it "nice guy" sometime and eat only berries and animal meat, but it need more dears and squirels, and even bunnies, rats, birds etc.. Traps also are underated, we should be able to put one in the forest and come back later to see if it caught something.
-Maps markers, like if i have to drop my loot for some reason, I can mark the place to come back later, this could combine with the previous traps comment to know where you had put a trap, and make you come back to check them before your catch get stolen (by a thief or another animal) or spoils.
-More detailed medicinal interraction: risks of local wound infection (that can turn to septisemia of not cured), specific intervention required (tools needed to pull out an arrow, suturation, hemoragy, broken bones etc.)
-Difficulty choice/save game, as it's pretty frustrating to start all over everytime you die, i'd personnally like to be able to save my games at some points, maybe make it hard like having to find a saving location in the map etc.  An alternative would be to propose 2 game modes: hardcore (permadeath) and softcore (respaw with penalties).
-Zombies, lol joke, the game is allready great, it doesn't even need zombies (i'm not sure some zombie-like creatures would ruin it tho).
That's about all I can think of right now, but anyway the game rocks! I really hope you guys will push it to the best of it's potential, and for the players still hesitating: go for it! It's worth every penny!

Mathematically, since Blender is free, you get an infinitely better deal than purchasing commercial software.
Now for serious reviewing. One of the great things is that it can play any part in the 3D process, whether that be video editing, compositing, modelling, animation, or even rendering. However, the flip side of this is that not all of the features can be equally fleshed out. In Blender's case, the modelling, physics, and rendering components recieve a decent amount of attention, whereas other things such as video editing and game logic editing could use more work. Also, all of that has to be packed into one bundle of software. Blender has made an OK interface where you can divide the main window into seperate smaller sections, and open a certain component of Blender in each section, such as image viewing or object properties. This interface could use some work, though, since more and more capability has been crammed into existing sections. Andrew Price, a well-known maker of Blender tutorials, now heads a group of developers trying to improve the organization and de-clusterizing the workspace.
Blender also relies heavily on keyboard shortcuts. For example, Shift+A brings up a list of objects that can be added to the scene. It can take a while to get the hang of these shortcuts (especially obscure ones like shift+ctrl+alt+c to set an object's origin) though the search feature (space) can help you easily find a particular tool, and will remind you of the keyboard shortcut associated with it.
The modelling system is quite fleshed out. You can do lots of things in it, from simple things like filling holes, to more complex things such as the 'subdivision surface' modifier. UV mapping works quite well. You can mark where the mesh should be 'cut' (imagine seams on clothing) to make a flat image, or, (if you're feeling lazy) you can have Blender dynamically cut the mesh for you.
The render engine is quite good. Blender's most used render engine (there are 3, not counting the standard OpenGL renderer, which is used for the 3D view) is Cycles. Cycles is a ray-based engine, meaning that it actually calculates rays of light, and how they bounce off or go through certain objects. This can be very realistic (especially with the variety of free materials available) but it does have downsides. Be warned, Cycles usually takes a long time to render a nice-looking image. (though a decent GPU can increase the render times up to 15x) The internal renderer (AKA 'Blender Render') can work faster, though it is not very flexible and takes practice to be able to produce realistic results.
I haven't touched the game logic, and neither have many other people. From what I've heard, it's a fairly poorly implemented system. Unfortunately, Blender was
made to create games. If you're looking for something to make games with, you will have to look somewhere else.
One great thing about Blender is its open movies. A group of Blender people will get together and try and make a film. Though they turn out to be very good-looking, emotionally-compelling videos, there's another great thing about them. When someone makes an open film, the Blender devs are keeping an eye on them, seeing what features they need. By putting Blender to the test, they can see what needs to be added, taken away, or revamped. This usually makes Blender more feature-rich and useable. One of these films, created by the Mango Project (they're all named after fruit) actually added chroma keying (green screen) and motion tracking into Blender.
That's about all I can think of, I hope you find it useful.

Let me preface this. I never liked the idea of Telltale Games. I don't consider them games, just a story you can sometimes control. I am not a fan of this genre.
BUT, it's Game Of Thrones and it was on sale. So I said, "screw it", and bought it.
I was PLEASANTLY surprised.
Pros:
Story is mostly solid with plenty of characters I came to enjoy.
Some decisions were hard and reminds me of The Witcher 3; there is no real "happy" ending depending on your sense of "happy".
Cameos are not overdone and are voice acted by the actual actors. Your stories run quite parallel to most of the main Game Of Thrones series story, only intersecting a few times, and those times are well done.
Cons:
You will hate me for picking on this, but, GRAPHICS. I don't mind stylized graphics, but on 4k resultion, the graphics get a little funky and it oddly looks better on 1080p.
Some background audio awkwardly overtakes main character audio at times. This is a pain for someone like me who plays without subtitles.
No real combat, just quick time events. The QTE's are also too forgiving. If you press X instead of Y, nothing happens unless you press Y. Other games will count X as the button and thus you fail the QTE. Sometimes it doesn't matter if you complete the QTE at all because the game decides to save you anyway.
This isn't really a con, but, the game still has a second season to come out and the ending of episode 6 is a huge cliffhanger. Though I look eager to the new stuff, I heard things that it will come out in pieces in 2018.

I've been using Blender on and off for the last year or so, but only recently did I get serious about learning it, since I work for a small game developer and we are stuck with an old, and very buggy version of Maya. Although I've been into open source an free software for some time, I found it difficult to get used to Blender's UI because I was so used to Maya, and had kind of dismissed it as weird and difficult to learn. It was not until I really tried to switch to Blender and properly learned the UI that I realised that I was merely being inflexible, and Blender is not weird once you get the hang of things.
Once you get over the initial hump, which is likely only something users of other 3d software will encounter, you will find an extremely powerful, full featured and STABLE 3d program, that can handle a huge variety of tasks up to production quality required for professional games and cg animations. Some of the things that Blender can do, such as fluid dynamics, cloth simulation, compositing and motion tracking are only available in commercial software through addons, or by buying other software, but Blender handles all of these tasks quite well.
Perhaps the best thing about Blender, however, is that it has a friendly community of users and developers, so if you need help, it's usually very easy to get. There are also a lot of good quality and free learning materials, as well as a few paid sites that do a great job of teaching more advanced topics.
Oh, and being free means that you will always have the latest version, as well as unrestricted access to all previous versions and their source code. I don't know how anyone couldn't love Blender - as long as they give it a chance!

Throwing off the burden of age is hard enough for most games we hold dear without choking on thier own legacy and exposing the flaws we once were willfully ignorant of. But not for this titan of a game which weaves the best mechanics from action and RTS games ensuring freshness combined with timeless fun. Leading the impressive, hulking Blood Ravens proves to be a thrilling experience which excercises a brain that often switches off thanks to overly simplistic modern games. Using the lore of 40K like a paintbrush benefits the game in every regard, the  strong character design of each race to the BRILLIANT voice acting, finishing off with a stimulating, richly composed soundtrack. Being a old school RTS player, the ripping out off micromanagement was a concern unfounded because finding myself as involved with the fates of my units rather then a multitude of speadsheets was a welcome break. Anyone looking fior a fun, enjoyable introduction to RTS, buy this game ASAP.

The combat system is one that sticks out. It's somewhat reminiscent of the original Wasteland, but instead of a hit point system, damage is actually done to the combantants.The commands are a little more complex than a lot of systems, if you're knocked down, for instance, you can either get up, roll away, or grab the enemy by the ankles and pull 'em down. Most combat is completely optional too, you can sneak away, talk your way out of it, or simply avoid it in general.
Plenty of skills and flaws are selectable from the start, and more skills are able to be obtained later in the game. This encourages trial and error, which is more acceptable in this, considering the survival mechanics, as opposed to a more traditional RPG with cutscenes and dungeons you have to go through in the beginning. Speaking of survival mechanics, they're fantastic; this game is the survival game I've been waiting for. Food and water can be obtained in a myriad of ways. The crafting system is really general, so materials can usually be substituted for others, as opposed to needing very specific things.
The quite clear flaw to all this (at least to some people) is almost unavoidable, and it's that it's not a casual-friendly experience. It's not extremely hard to get into, but a lack of experience and foresight is bound to get you killed on occasion. The randomness of your start also might decide your fate more-so than your skill, depending on the direction you go, but this was either pretty easy to bounce back from, or simply rare.
If you like survival games, or late-eighties CRPGs like Wasteland, than you'll find a pretty polished combination that's certain to pull quite a few hours out of you.

Wow... what to say about XCOM: Enemy Unknown? It took me 36 hours to complete the game (after one false start), and that day and a half I devoted to saving planet Earth was so incredibly fun that I had a hard time putting it down (just one more turn... just one more mission...). And so incredibly frustrating... yet somehow, even when I ragequit because I did something stupid and got one of my soldiers killed, I was back up and playing within 15 minutes because I wanted to keep playing.
XCOM:EU is a turn-based tactics game, which means you have to plan ahead and play things smart if you want to keep your squad alive. And even if you come up with the perfect strategy, odds are, something will go terribly wrong and your soldiers will die a terrible death anyway (and you might get attached to your soldiers, so don't do that). Even though it isn't a fast-paced game, boy, does it get tense sometimes. Personally, I find real-time strategy games a bit overwhelming, so it struck a perfect balance for me.
I play on a rather low-end system (integrated Intel HD 400 graphics on a i3 processor) and the game ran great, barring a few choppy cutscenes. Always a plus.
I loved being able to customize my soldiers, although I wish there were a few more choices... after a while, everyone started to look and sound the same despite my best attempts to avoid it. The Enemy Within expansion included a bunch of foreign language voices to pick from, which helps break the monotony).
The story was very enjoyable. I know a lot of people felt that XCOM:EU was too "on the rails", but I like that the game was driven forward by plot events. It didn't feel rushed or too drawn out, especially with the missions and plotlines added in the DLC (Admittedly, I feel like some parts could have been developed further-- mae a bit more in-depth).
I wish there were more games done in the style of XCOM:EU, because I love the genre, the gameplay, and the concept of controlling my own little squad and watching them progress and grow stronger (and cry when they are mauled by a pack of Chrysalids and gunned down by their mind-controlled squadmate... but I digress).
XCOM:EU was my first foray into the world of XCOM, having never played any of the original games released in the 90s. So I can't really say how XCOM:EU compares to the other titles in the series. There was no nostalgia for me; XCOM was a brand new experience for me (I have played Xenonauts, but it's like comparing homemade cookies to an ice cream sundae. One is a little fancier, but they are both really good; it just depends on what you are in the mood for). And what an experience it was... possibly one of my favorite games. If you have not tried it yet, and are intrigued by the idea of blasting aliens of the planet or like squad-based games... really, give it try.

There are probably 5-6 paragraphs I could write about why exactly this game is great, but I'll try and just cover a few that come to mind first. In summary the game is a sequel to Titan Quest that also feels like a sequel to Diablo 2, but expanding the whole concept by about 3-4x the level of sophistication and depth. I'm talking about dual-classing mixed with a secondary skill tree, ~10 damage types to build strategies around, parity between melee, caster, summoner, and ranged build-types, and tons of interesting skills. Since you can dual cast you don't have that issue where you miss 1 thing about 1 class that you really like while playing another class. You can mix and match how many points you invest within two classes. For example in Diablo 2 the Sorcereress could teleport which was such an amazing ability but if you wanted to play an Amazon you couldn't use teleport to the same extent (you could use items a bit but thats beside the point), here you could make a Sorceress-Amazon hybrid that uses teleport and energy shield mixed with a bow if you wanted for instance.
It's a really great game, think Diablo 2 but with a degree of Baldurs-Gate 2 level agency where you have some choices regarding which factions to support and how to interact with NPCs. Universal dual-classing adds a nicer level of sophistication to the game than Diablo 3 did, imagine combining a Sorcereress with a Barbarian for example.
This game has one of the best 'Summoner' Experiences I've ever seen, there are 3 classes with a Summoner focus- the Shaman, Occultist, and Necromancer. You can control your pets mid-battle using the "Pet Attack" command and can create varied armies of up to 25 minions. Since you dual class you can make interesting army compositions if you want a Summoner experience, for example you can synergize woodland spirits with skeletons, or demons with skeletons, or demons with woodland spirits.
The game also has one of the best caster vs auto attack balances where everything just uses weapon damage, and you can convert damage types between one of ~10 damage types with gear or spells to make full use of +% elemental damage buffs. In D3 this became really tedious since you had to only stack ONE damage type and each spell had it's own element, here you can convert your cold to fire if you really want, or physical to 'vitality' (one of the damage types). And so on.
The game has about ~100 hours of content to go through per playthrough, and you increase the difficulty each time you beat the game. They are just coming out with some D3-style end game content in the form of expansions so you can continue your adventure after beating the game on the hardest difficulty. There is a shared stash for all your characters as well as some level of universal faction advancement across all characters where you can basically double the faction progress for new playthroughs once you have played extensively with one character. This makes having multiple characters less tedious and more fun, while having a level of challenge with your initial playthrough.

A must have : one of the most powerful 3D software available, free, open source and always evolving... When a cool new feature appears on other 3D softwares, you get it for free on Blender just a few monthes later... Modeling, painting, animating, realtime rendering, there is nothing Blender can't do ! It's well coded (in Python), robust and flexible, very lightweight on hardware and works flawlessly on PC, Mac and Linux. Even with a modest computer, you can do incredible things !
It can even replace some editing and compositing softwares as it works on layers and can be integrated into many workflows. The motion tracker is very good also, and Cycles rendering is quite exemplary (lightning fast, with GPU rendering !).
Just as with all advanced 3D softwares, you need to ingest hours of tutorials to master the basics and pass over its major drawback : its ergonomy, which is, let's say "special" (not that bad, just very different from the others)...
After that, when you get it mastered, it's a marvelous tools, which never stops amazing me, every day, I'm serious :-)

What I played: Super Amazing Wagon Adventure
What I expected: A super amazing wagon adventure
What I got: A sporadic impossible wagon adventure
This game is a lot harder than I had anticipated; your hitbox is the entire wagon, making it tricky to avoid incoming things. You can only fire directly in front of you, making it sometimes difficult to shoot incoming enemies that clip the edges of your wagon.
The controls were a bit hard to get used to at first; you move with WASD and press the spacebar (or mouse button) to shoot, but in scenes where you're walking around outside the wagon, the game plays like a top-down shooter like The Binding of Isaac, Hotline Miami, Nuclear Throne, etc. in that you move with WASD and shoot with the four directional arrow keys (or use the mouse cursor for more versatile accuracy). Of course, all these controls can be remapped as you desire, and even comes with gamepad support if you want to use a controller.
Overall, this game refuses to take itself seriously, so why should you? This game is understandingly hard and it's easy to get frustrated, but given the nature of the game and how it's executed, I can't help but laugh every time I inevitably lose.

I never expected to live Grim Dawn. It’s a fairly straightforward Diablo-style run around and beat em up ARPG with all the class picking, spell-getting, “maybe if I do this area I can have a shirt with an extra 2 punching points” kind of click festival. But it does a few things just so much better than its contemporaries.
You pick 2 classes and mash them together. There’s more than 1 and usually more than 2 ways to effectively build any given class combination. The loot is variable enough to feel less like an interminable slog and more like that cherry on top of the grind sundae.  And the classic grim dark storyline is grim and dark and grim and dark and grim until the very end where you save the world, but it leaves just enough space for the right moments of levity.
All in all, I’m super glad to have got this game and all it’s DLC and if you like Diablos type games, you will be too.

At first glance FTL did not appeal to me. It's pixelated artstyle didn't appear sleak or particulary creative and the gameplay seemed haphazard and confusing. I couldn't have been more wrong, I love FTL! This game has deep and satisfying gameplay, offering elements of stragegy, action, resource management and risk vs. reward style choices at any given moment. What looks like a poor visual interface to the uninitiated, is actually a detailed and carefully crafted demonstration of a "less is more" artstyle. I couldn't picture this game looking any different now that I've played in 30 plus hours and I really appreciate it's subtlety in design. The gameplay and pacing are excellent, you can finish this game in 30mins or less with a little luck and a clear strategy. However, the events are random and vary from playthrough to playthrough which gives FTL amazing replayablity. One attempt, you might choose to explore an uncharted nebula in hopes of encountering alien homeworlds which can unlock new spacecraft and upgrades for future playthroughs. Another, you could be boarded by pirates and die in the first sector, lol. FTL's story is set in a familiar "space sci-fi" setting but establishes it's own distinctive lore. Most importantly, the game is fun! An excellent value at under $10, as low as $3 during sales. A must play that will certainly provide hours of enjoyment for anyone who is a fan of the space genre.
